builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: AgentBouncer: Defending Software Engineering Agents via Dynamic System-Call Mediation
summary: AgentBouncer replaces prompt- and trajectory-level defenses, which inspect only the initial prompt and tool-call sequence, with an LLM arbiter that mediates the actual system calls an agent triggers, gated by preseeded policy rules and hierarchy-aware caching. It costs about 47 seconds and USD 0.0036 per benign task, plus the engineering effort of integrating a syscall-interception layer into the agent's tool execution path. It can fail against attacks outside its evaluated four vectors, through arbiter misjudgment of necessity or safety on novel tasks, and if cache hits silently propagate an incorrect prior allow/deny decision.
rationale: Runtime system-call mediation is deployable on constrained infrastructure via API-hosted LLM arbitration, but its security claims rest on one custom attack dataset and require validation against the reader's own agent stack before production adoption.
technique: LLM-mediated system-call interception for agent defense

claims.statement: AgentBouncer replaces prompt- and trajectory-level defenses, which inspect only the initial prompt and tool-call sequence, with an LLM arbiter that mediates the actual system calls an agent triggers, gated by preseeded policy rules and hierarchy-aware caching. It costs about 47 seconds and USD 0.0036 per benign task, plus the engineering effort of integrating a syscall-interception layer into the agent's tool execution path. It can fail against attacks outside its evaluated four vectors, through arbiter misjudgment of necessity or safety on novel tasks, and if cache hits silently propagate an incorrect prior allow/deny decision.
Reduces attack success rate from 99.41% (undefended) to 10.59%, with 0.25% failed benign tool calls and USD 0.0036 plus 47 s added per benign task.
